# Relay stage 3: Diagnose
Task: fix-lossy-flagged-work-snapshot
Working directory: /tmp/nix-shell.L5haGz/visual-relay/wt/fbb5c78605a5/plan-20260706214512/fix-lossy-flagged-work-snapshot

## Task input
# Fix the Lossy Flagged-Work Snapshot and Restore

Resuming a flagged task corrupts the working tree. Observed on 2026-07-06: clicking **Resume** on a
flagged task restored its flagged-work bundle and thereby (a) **deleted the tracked
`.relay/config.json` and `.relay/.gitignore`** — the app then showed the "Initialize this project"
screen because config.json was gone — and (b) **stripped the executable bit** from
`.githooks/command-guard`, `.githooks/commit-msg`, `.githooks/pre-commit`, `test.sh`, `me.sh`,
`tools/dotnet-test-files.sh`, and `visual-relay`. The de-executabled command-guard then made every
stage-8 attempt die in ~6 seconds with `swival exit 1: Error: command_middleware executable not
found or not executable: …/.githooks/command-guard`, burning all retries and escalations
(run 3/3, attempts 1–10) in about a minute before re-flagging. Make the snapshot/restore
round-trip faithful: tracked `.relay/` files and file modes must survive.

## Current state (researched)

- `src/VisualRelay.Core/Execution/FlaggedWorkStore.cs` `CaptureAsync` builds the kill-time
  snapshot in a **fresh temporary index** (`GIT_INDEX_FILE` pointed at a new path):
  1. `git add -A` stages everything;
  2. `git rm --cached -r -q --ignore-unmatch -- .relay/` then de-indexes ALL `.relay/` paths;
  3. `write-tree` / `commit-tree -p <runBaseSha>` produce the snapshot commit.
- **Defect 1 (deletions):** step 2's intent is to keep runtime relay metadata out of the bundle,
  but `.relay/config.json` and `.relay/.gitignore` are **tracked at the run base**, so removing
  them from the index makes the snapshot tree record them as *deleted* relative to base.
  `RestoreAsync` applies the snapshot with `git cherry-pick -n <snapshotSha>`, which faithfully
  deletes them from the working tree on resume.
- **Defect 2 (modes):** populating a **brand-new empty index** with `git add -A` under
  `core.fileMode=false` records every path as `100644` — there is no prior index entry to carry
  the mode, and git does not read modes from disk in that configuration. Verified: the run base
  has `100755` for `.githooks/command-guard`, `test.sh`, and `visual-relay`; the captured
  snapshot tree has `100644` for all of them. The cherry-pick then chmods the working files.
  (This repo had `core.fileMode=false` from a VM-shared-folder era; it has since been unset, but
  capture must be robust on any clone where it is false.)
- Restore call site: `RelayDriver.FlaggedWork.cs` ("On resume, restores the flagged working tree
  from a flagged-work bundle"). Why the exec bit matters: `SwivalSubagentRunner.BuildArguments`
  (`ProcessRunners.cs`) passes `--command-middleware <root>/.githooks/command-guard` whenever the
  file exists, and swival refuses to start when it is not executable.
- Existing test surfaces: `tests/VisualRelay.Tests/RelayDriverResumeTests.FlaggedWork.cs` and
  `.FlaggedWork2.cs` (capture/restore behavior through the driver), plus the sidecar assertions
  mentioned in `FlaggedWorkStore.cs`. There is no test covering tracked-`.relay` preservation or
  mode fidelity.

## What to build (TDD-first)

1. **Tests first** (extend `RelayDriverResumeTests.FlaggedWork*.cs` or add a focused
   `FlaggedWorkStoreTests.cs` using the same repo fixtures): a capture→restore round-trip on a
   test repo that has (a) a tracked `.relay/config.json` committed at base, (b) a tracked
   executable script (`100755` at base), and (c) `core.fileMode=false` set in the repo config.
   After capture on a dirty tree and restore onto a fresh checkout of base:
   - `.relay/config.json` still exists with its base content (never recorded as deleted);
   - the script's index/tree mode is still `100755` and the working file is executable;
   - the task's real edits are present (the existing behavior keeps working).
2. **Fix capture's `.relay/` handling** in `CaptureAsync`: instead of `git rm --cached -r --
   .relay/`, reset the `.relay/` paths in the temp index back to the run base's versions (e.g.
   `git restore --source=<runBaseSha> --staged -- .relay/` under the same `GIT_INDEX_FILE`
   environment, or an equivalent `ls-tree`-driven re-add of exactly the tracked-at-base `.relay/`
   entries). Result: the snapshot tree's `.relay/` content equals the base's, so the cherry-pick
   diff contains no `.relay/` changes at all — runtime metadata still never enters the bundle,
   and nothing gets deleted on restore.
3. **Fix capture's mode fidelity**: seed the temp index from the run base **before** staging
   (`git read-tree <runBaseSha>` with the `GIT_INDEX_FILE` environment, then `git add -A`) so
   tracked files carry their base modes through `add` even under `core.fileMode=false`, and/or
   run the capture-side `add` with `-c core.fileMode=true` so real on-disk bits are honored where
   the filesystem supports them. Either way the round-trip test in (1) must pass with
   `core.fileMode=false` set.
4. **Belt-and-braces on restore** (small, optional if (2)+(3) prove sufficient): after a
   successful cherry-pick in `RestoreAsync`, verify `.relay/config.json` still exists when it
   existed before the restore, and surface a loud failure (`RestoreResult`-level, not silent)
   instead of proceeding into a run with a deleted config.

## Done when

- The round-trip test proves: tracked `.relay/` files survive restore byte-for-byte, executable
  modes survive capture+restore under `core.fileMode=false`, and the task's actual edits are
  restored as before.
- Existing resume/flagged-work tests still pass; `./visual-relay check` passes (file-size guard,
  format verification, build, full test suite, README screenshot render).

## Guardrails

- Conventional Commits only (the `commit-msg` hook enforces the full ruleset). See
  `docs/commit-messages.md` and `AGENTS.md`.
- `FlaggedWorkStore.cs` is 253 lines — stay under the 300-line guard (extract a partial like the
  existing `FlaggedWorkStore` partial split if needed).
- All git operations must remain harness-side plumbing through `IGitInvoker` — no shelling out
  around it, no hook bypasses (matches the file's existing doc comment).
- Do not change the bundle format/ref layout (`refs/relay-snapshot/<taskId>`, sidecar JSON) —
  existing bundles on disk should still restore; only their `.relay`/mode defects go away for
  newly captured ones.
- Minimal diffs: change only what this task needs; do not reformat or reflow unrelated code.

Now I have all the evidence. Let me compose the final diagnostic:

```json
{
  "evidence": "## Defect 1: Tracked `.relay/` files deleted on restore

**Root cause**: `FlaggedWorkStore.cs` line 64–65:
```csharp
_ = await gitInvoker.RunAsync(
    rootPath, ["rm", "--cached", "-r", "-q", "--ignore-unmatch", "--", ".relay/"], ct, environment: env);
```
This `git rm --cached -r -- .relay/` strips ALL `.relay/` entries from the temp index, *including those tracked at the run base*. The intent (comment on line 62–63) is to "unstage .relay/ files so the snapshot does not include the bundle or any other git-ignored relay metadata" — but the implementation is too broad.

**Which files are tracked at the run base**:
```
$ git ls-tree HEAD .relay/
.relay/.gitignore                                          (100644)
.relay/config.json                                         (100644)
.relay/control-api-index-page/                             (tree — many tracked files)
.relay/diagnose-stage-evidence-only/                       (tree — many tracked files)
.relay/update-readme-to-make-install-faster/               (tree — many tracked files)
```

**How the snapshot records them as deleted**:
- Line 58: `git add -A` stages everything (including all `.relay/` files) into the fresh temp index.
- Line 64–65: `git rm --cached -r -- .relay/` removes them from the temp index.
- Line 76: `git write-tree` produces a tree that has NO `.relay/` entries.
- Line 84: `git commit-tree <treeSha> -p <runBaseSha>` creates a commit where `.relay/` entries are absent from the tree — git interprets this as deletion relative to the parent.

**How restore applies the deletions**:
- Line 170–171: `git cherry-pick -n <snapshotSha>` applies the snapshot commit's diff onto HEAD. Since the snapshot tree has no `.relay/` entries, the diff says "delete `.relay/config.json`", "delete `.relay/.gitignore`", etc., and cherry-pick faithfully removes them from the working tree.

**Observed impact**: After resume, `.relay/config.json` is gone, so the app shows the "Initialize this project" screen (no config → uninitialized state).

## Defect 2: Executable bit stripped on restore under `core.fileMode=false`

**Root cause**: `FlaggedWorkStore.cs` lines 52–58:
```csharp
var tempIndex = Path.Combine(Path.GetTempPath(), $"git-index-{Guid.NewGuid():N}");
var env = new Dictionary<string, string>(StringComparer.Ordinal)
{
    ["GIT_INDEX_FILE"] = tempIndex
};
var addResult = await gitInvoker.RunAsync(rootPath, ["add", "-A"], ct, environment: env);
```
A brand-new empty temp index is used. There are NO prior index entries to carry mode information. When `core.fileMode=false` is set in the repo config, `git add -A` records every file as `100644` — git does not read the executable bit from disk in that configuration.

**Which files ARE executable at base** (`git ls-files --stage`):
```
100755 .githooks/command-guard
100755 .githooks/commit-msg
100755 .githooks/pre-commit
100755 test.sh
100755 me.sh
100755 tools/dotnet-test-files.sh
100755 visual-relay
```

**What the snapshot tree would record**: All `100644` (verified in research: the run base has `100755` for these files but the captured snapshot tree gets `100644` — there is no prior index entry and `core.fileMode=false` prevents git from reading on-disk modes).

**How restore strips the +x**: `git cherry-pick -n` applies the mode change from `100755` (base) to `100644` (snapshot), chmodding the working files.

**Why it matters**: `ProcessRunners.cs` lines 115–119:
```csharp
var guardPath = Path.Combine(invocation.TargetRoot, ".githooks", "command-guard");
if (File.Exists(guardPath))
{
    args.Add("--command-middleware");
    args.Add(guardPath);
}
```
Swival refuses to start when `command-guard` is not executable, causing every stage-8 attempt to die in ~6 seconds with `swival exit 1: Error: command_middleware executable not found or not executable: …/.githooks/command-guard`.",
  "excerpts": [
    "FlaggedWorkStore.cs:64-65 — `git rm --cached -r -q --ignore-unmatch -- .relay/` strips ALL .relay/ paths from temp index, including tracked-at-base files",
    "FlaggedWorkStore.cs:52-58 — brand-new empty temp index + `git add -A` under core.fileMode=false records everything as 100644",
    "FlaggedWorkStore.cs:76 — `write-tree` produces snapshot tree from the lossy temp index",
    "FlaggedWorkStore.cs:84 — `commit-tree -p <runBaseSha>` creates snapshot commit where missing .relay/ entries = deletions relative to base",
    "FlaggedWorkStore.cs:170-171 — `git cherry-pick -n <snapshotSha>` faithfully applies deletions and mode-stripping to working tree",
    "ProcessRunners.cs:115-119 — `--command-middleware .githooks/command-guard` passed to swival when file exists; swival refuses to start if not executable",
    "RelayDriver.FlaggedWork.cs:32-33 — RestoreAsync called on resume; no guard checking .relay/config.json existence after restore",
    ".relay/.gitignore:6-8 — `*` with `!.gitignore` and `!config.json` exceptions — runtime metadata is git-ignored but those two files are tracked",
    "git ls-files --stage .githooks/command-guard etc.: confirmed 100755 at base for all githook scripts, test.sh, me.sh, visual-relay",
    "git ls-tree HEAD .relay/: confirmed .relay/config.json (100644) and .relay/.gitignore (100644) plus task subdirectories are tracked at HEAD"
  ],
  "repro": "## Reproduce Defect 1 (tracked .relay/ deleted)

```bash
# Setup: fresh repo with tracked .relay/config.json
cd $(mktemp -d)
git init -b main
git config user.email test@test
git config user.name Test
mkdir -p .relay
echo '{"testCmd":"true"}' > .relay/config.json
echo '*
!.gitignore
!config.json' > .relay/.gitignore
git add .relay/config.json .relay/.gitignore
git commit -m "initial"
RUN_BASE=$(git rev-parse HEAD)

# Simulate CaptureAsync's temp-index workflow
export GIT_INDEX_FILE=$(mktemp)
git add -A
git rm --cached -r -q --ignore-unmatch -- .relay/  # <-- DEFECT: strips tracked .relay/ files
TREE=$(git write-tree)
SNAP=$(git commit-tree $TREE -p $RUN_BASE -m "snapshot")

# The snapshot tree has no .relay/ entries
git ls-tree $SNAP .relay/  # empty output → .relay/config.json recorded as deleted

# Verify the diff shows deletion
git diff-tree --name-status $RUN_BASE $SNAP .relay/  # shows D .relay/config.json, D .relay/.gitignore

# Cleanup
rm $GIT_INDEX_FILE
```

## Reproduce Defect 2 (executable modes lost under core.fileMode=false)

```bash
# Setup: fresh repo with executable script + core.fileMode=false
cd $(mktemp -d)
git init -b main
git config user.email test@test
git config user.name Test
git config core.fileMode false  # <-- the defect scenario
echo '#!/bin/sh
echo hi' > script.sh
chmod +x script.sh
git add script.sh
git commit -m "initial"
RUN_BASE=$(git rev-parse HEAD)

# Base has 100755
git ls-files --stage script.sh  # 100755 ...

# Simulate CaptureAsync: fresh temp index + add -A under core.fileMode=false
export GIT_INDEX_FILE=$(mktemp)
git add -A
git ls-files --stage script.sh  # 100644 ...  <-- DEFECT: executable bit lost
TREE=$(git write-tree)
SNAP=$(git commit-tree $TREE -p $RUN_BASE -m "snapshot")
git ls-tree $SNAP script.sh  # 100644 blob ...  <-- snapshot recorded as non-executable

# Cleanup
rm $GIT_INDEX_FILE
```"
}
```
